cards.explanation: The answer is one foot on the sea and one on the land. The angel "…placed his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land." (Revelation 10:2) One foot in the water, one foot on the ground, and a little scroll lying open in his hand. I stay put on my gold base, friends, and I still wobble when the floor gets sticky.

The answer is False. John was about to write it down, and then the voice from heaven stopped him. It said, “Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down.” (Revelation 10:4) So John kept it sealed. I can't even keep a cookie recipe to myself, friends, and he kept thunder.

The answer is False. The angel lifts his right hand to heaven and swears by “…Him who lives forever and ever…” (Revelation 10:6) That's the One who created heaven, the earth and the sea, and everything in them. The thunders spoke earlier, but he doesn't swear by them.

The answer is that there will be no more delay. The angel says, “There will be no more delay!” (Revelation 10:6) He swears it by the One who created everything, so he's saying it with his hand raised. I wish my oven timer sounded that sure of itself, friends.

The answer is the mystery of God. The angel says that when the seventh angel begins to sound his trumpet, “…the mystery of God will be fulfilled…” (Revelation 10:7) I'm not going to guess past that, friends, because the text doesn't. I just keep my ovens ready.

The answer is His servants the prophets. The mystery of God will be fulfilled “…just as He proclaimed to His servants the prophets.” (Revelation 10:7) So God said it first, and the angel says it's coming. That's a pretty good track record, bakers.

The answer is to take the small scroll from the angel. The voice says, “Go, take the small scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land.” (Revelation 10:8) That's a mighty angel to walk up to. I'd be rehearsing my "excuse me" the whole way over, friends.

The answer is that it makes his stomach bitter. The angel says, “It will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be as sweet as honey.” (Revelation 10:9) Sweet going down and bitter after. I've had a cookie like that once, friends, and I blame the raisins.

The answer is True. John says he ate it, “…and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth. But when I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter.” (Revelation 10:10) Same two things the angel told him (Revelation 10:9), just in the order John felt them. Nothing came out different, bakers.

The answer is to prophesy again about many peoples and kings. John is told, “You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and tongues and kings.” (Revelation 10:11) So the scroll isn't the end of his job, friends. It's more like the start of the next part. And the story isn't over yet.
